Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test case `testGetNode()` asserts that a node is selected from an XPath expression `"//vendor"` on a DOM model context. The current bug report indicates that descendant-or-self axis does not work correctly at the root node, specifically that for XML like `<root id="1234"/>` and XPath `"//root/@id/text()"`, JXPath returns null instead of the expected attribute text.

Walking through the code paths involved in `selectSingleNode(xpath)`:
- This calls `getPointer(xpath)` in `JXPathContextReferenceImpl`.
- `getPointer(String xpath)` compiles the expression and then calls `getPointer(String, Expression)`.
- `getPointer(String, Expression)` calls `expr.computeValue()` to get a result.
- If the result is an `EvalContext`, it extracts a single node pointer via `getSingleNodePointer()`.
- `getSingleNodePointer()` iterates over the set to return the first node pointer or null if none.

The problem likely lies in the evaluation of the descendant or self (`//`) axis on the root node. The XPath expression `"//root/@id/text()"` is meant to find all "root" elements anywhere descendants or self from the current root (document node). If JXPath does not properly consider the root node as part of the descendant-or-self axis, the expression returns null.

The `EvalContext` iteration (`nextSet()`, `nextNode()`) and the pointer retrieval steps suggest the candidate location of the bug is in the evaluation of the descendant-or-self axis or the node iteration at the root node. Possibly the root node is not included in the axis traversal in this context or the attribute/text nodes are not correctly visited starting from the root.

Since `DOMNodePointer.isActual()` always returns true, the pointer validity is not the cause here.

Recent bug reports about extensions and removal do not relate to this axis evaluation.

Hence the issue is that the descendant-or-self axis evaluation in JXPath does not properly include the root node itself resulting in failed selections on paths like `"//root/@id/text()"`.

The failing test `testGetNode()` demonstrates this symptom by selecting `"//vendor"` which would similarly fail if the root or descendants nodes are not traversed properly.

The root cause is the improper handling of the descendant-or-self axis starting at the root node in the XPath evaluation logic. This causes node pointer retrieval for such queries to fail, returning null instead of expected nodes or attribute/text values.

The places to fix would be in the expression evaluation logic for the descendant-or-self axis in the DOM node model or the EvalContext nextNode()/nextSet() iteration logic when starting from the root node in JXPathContextReferenceImpl or related classes in the DOM model.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
